A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VERICODE taxonomy, benchmark augmentation pipeline, model evaluation, and preference analysis. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite renaming and extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 31 LLMs, functionality and instruction-following measurements, positional analyses, and correlations with human preference.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds instruction-selection validation, category-specific measurements, and repeated-run stability results.

M1.justification: The 30-instruction taxonomy, selector, parameter validation, deterministic verifiers, and generation/editing procedures remain unchanged. Appendix verifier code and evaluation prompts are retained; SWE-IF is a renaming of Vibe Checker.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Python tasks from BigCodeBench and LiveCodeBench and use the same LMArena coding ratings. BigVibeBench and LiveVibeBench become Big-SWE-IF and Live-SWE-IF. The added audits and analyses use existing coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated 31-model cohort, 24-model LiveCodeBench subset, and Gemini 2.5 Pro versus Claude 4 Opus selector comparison are retained. The new analyses examine existing models without introducing or replacing comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix B.2 adds a human-validation protocol: two authors independently assess relevance and non-conflict for 500 instructions from 100 randomly sampled instances, equally divided between benchmarks. Existing benchmark sizes, prompts, metrics, temperatures, and interaction protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands supplementary analysis through instruction-selection validation, category-specific error profiles for seven leading models, and run-to-run stability checks (Appendices B.2, D.3, and D.5). Existing positional and preference analyses remain; new family-level plots also summarize retained evaluation results.

E5.justification: v1 provides no run-to-run uncertainty estimates. v2 explicitly adds five-run experiments and mean pass@1 with standard deviations for four Gemini models on Big-SWE-IF, across both interaction modes and instruction counts (Table 15). This is a localized addition; no formal significance test or uncertainty analysis of the preference correlations is reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds category-specific IF results, 100% relevance/non-conflict validity in the audited sample, and repeated-run outcomes (Tables 13–15 and Appendix B.2). Most existing scores remain unchanged. Table 7 revises single-turn Claude 4 Sonnet IF at three instructions from 81.37 to 81.90 and five instructions from 81.37 to 81.28; o4 mini at five instructions changes from 84.25 to 84.05.

T1.justification: The functional-regression formula, instruction-level and task-level IF definitions, and weighted preference score remain mathematically unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract drops the real-world-programming qualification when describing IF as the primary differentiator, instead saying 'among LLMs.' This slightly broadens the abstract's claim, although the introduction retains the qualification and the principal contributions and conclusions otherwise remain stable.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of selector reliability, category-specific model strengths, and run stability. New Appendix E explains function-level scope, limitations of deterministic checks for subjective requirements, and possible static-analysis errors; v1 chiefly noted Python scope and specific implementation caveats. Some new interpretations overgeneralize, including documentation being consistently the weakest category.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future release of the taxonomy and verifiers. v2 supplies a repository link and states that code, data, and taxonomy are available. Existing implementation code, prompts, API information, and model identifiers are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning against functional code benchmarks and non-verifiable instruction-following evaluations remain unchanged. Reference formatting and citation ordering change without adding a new research relationship.

P1.justification: v2 renames the paper and benchmarks, tightens wording, adds acknowledgements and an impact statement, removes the LLM Usage Statement, and updates appendix organization. The main six-section narrative and most existing prose are retained.

P2.justification: The single-column report becomes a two-column conference paper with substantially different typography, figure placement, and table sizing. Figure 1 is redrawn, Figure 12 is restyled, captions are expanded, and Tables 13–15 and Figures 16–17 are added. Retained appendix code and prompt illustrations are resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: The selection audit, category breakdowns, repeated-run checks, explicit limitations, and resource-access information improve support and transparency relative to v1. Gains remain limited: stability covers Gemini functionality on one benchmark, leaving preference-correlation uncertainty unaddressed. New interpretation also occasionally overreaches: Table 14 reports Kimi K2 logic IF of 49.62 versus documentation IF of 73.23, contradicting the claim that documentation is consistently weakest.
